div.div:
Basic information
Name, Description
Slug default-openai — what the app names in the call
Credential stays here, never handed out
OpenAI API key. Optional fields on this page may include
Organization ID and Project ID; fill them if your account uses them.
Model provisioning
All models, or an explicit allowlist. Everything not on the list is
unreachable through this integration, which is how you keep an
expensive reasoning model out of a chatbot's reach.
Workspace provisioning
Which teams see OpenAI in their Model Catalog, and each team's
budget and rate limit.
Pricing adjust multiplier
Your negotiated OpenAI rate, or an internal showback markup.

div.b: The gateway fronts the OpenAI API. It cannot front the ChatGPT app.

div.div:
ChatGPT in a browser, the desktop app, and the mobile app have no base
URL setting. There is nothing to point at a gateway, so that traffic never
reaches Observability and no budget, allowlist, or guardrail touches it.
When a customer says "we use ChatGPT", establish which one they mean:
• Code calling api.openai.com — an SDK, an agent framework, a
CI job. This is what the gateway covers, and it is the whole point.
• People typing into chatgpt.com — covered by network egress
policy, a CASB or SASE control, or ChatGPT Enterprise's own admin
and compliance tooling. Not by the AI Gateway.
The same split applies to Claude.ai against the Anthropic API, and to a
Copilot surface against the Azure endpoint behind it. Naming the split on
the first call avoids a scope argument at cutover, because "we are
governing our AI usage" means two different projects.

div.div:
1. OpenAI bills your OpenAI account for inference. Unchanged by the
gateway. Same key, same rates, same platform usage dashboard.
2. Palo Alto Networks meters flex credits by token volume.
1 token = 4 characters. Prompts, MCP, and agent-to-agent traffic all
count. Identical pricing for SaaS and Hybrid.
Because every call now carries one key, the OpenAI usage dashboard
collapses to a single line. Per-team and per-app breakdown moves into
the gateway logs, and depends entirely on your key metadata.

div.div:
Grounded in the repository guides and the PAN reference page. Web
research was blocked in this session, so none of it was checked externally:
• Whether the details page exposes Organization ID and Project ID as
named fields, or expects a key that already carries that scope.
• Which OpenAI endpoints are proxied. Chat completions is safe to
assume; Responses, Assistants, Batch, and Realtime are not.
• Whether an OpenAI-compatible self-hosted model (vLLM, Ollama) uses
this integration with a Custom Host, or a different provider entry.
• Whether streaming responses are logged in full or summarized.
